text:
ana: quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector change from 'latency-first' -> 'balanced' we saw a regression on the similarity embedding endpoint. QPS dropped and token-level p99 climbed. anyone watching? :eyes:

sam: checking now. I already pulled a flamegraph from the gpu-host profiler. looks like kernel queue wait jumped and KV cache hit-rate dipped for some traffic buckets. pasting short excerpt:

```
route=/v1/embeddings/similarity
before: qps=235 med_lat=34ms p99_token=95ms kv_hit=0.72 batch_size=8
after:  qps=182 med_lat=48ms p99_token=128ms kv_hit=0.58 batch_size=8
kernel_queue_wait_ms +42%  | kernel_dispatch_time +8% | io_stalls +12%
```

sam: hypothesis: selector moved a chunk of requests to a kernel variant that's higher throughput for long sequences but worse for short sequences (our rerank/emb traffic is short, dim=768).

ravi: fwiw the reranker routes have lots of small batches (1-4 requests). batching heuristic changed to be more aggressive about waiting to reach batch size=8; that interacts badly with short tails. maybe increase adaptive timeout?

miles: I also see a KV-cache cold-start blip in both dev and prod — a rollout of the new model version invalidated some prefix keys. kv_hit_rate by prefix shows a few high-cardinality prefixes dropped from ~0.9 -> 0.4 for ~3min. could explain part of token p99.

ana: @sam can you share the per-stage token latency breakdown (tokenization -> kernel_queue -> kernel_exec -> postproc)? we want to instrument this on the dashboard.

sam: pasted quick breakdown from trace samples (short requests only):
```
stage: tokenization 3-5ms
stage: kernel_queue 10-38ms  (high variance after selector change)
stage: kernel_exec 8-12ms
stage: postproc 2-4ms
```

sam: so kernel_queue is the dominant delta. two levers: revert kernel-selector patch, or adjust batching/timeouts + kernel mapping policy (prefer low-lat kernel for short seqs).

ravi: my vote is try a conservative selector for the similarity route and increase batch-size cap to 16 for embeddings/vectors-only traffic, plus reduce adaptive wait to 8ms for rerank. that'll keep throughput while lowering queue wait.

miles: agree but we should also add a per-route KPI panel: tokens_per_stage, kernel_queue_wait_ms percentile, kv_hit_rate, batch_size_distribution, and qps_by_model_variant. I'll add a Grafana PR.

perf-bot: perf-alert triggered: route=/v1/embeddings/similarity p99_token_latency increased 34% | autotag: kernel-selector-2026-03-17

ana: next steps: 1) @sam roll a conservative mapping for /v1/embeddings/similarity to the previous kernel variant (canary 10% -> 50% -> rollback if safe) 2) @ravi tweak batching params for rerank routes (timeout 8ms, max_batch 16) 3) @miles add token-level panels and an alert on kernel_queue_wait_p99>100ms 4) add a perf regression test in CI that runs a short embedding QPS sweep (dim=768, batch sizes [1,4,8,16]) and records token breakdowns

sam: will do canary now and post results. starting 10% -> 50% if stable.

ravi: I'll prepare the batching patch and test on staging. expect a PR in ~30m.

miles: creating dashboard PR, will include pre/post traces + aggregated percentiles. linking when ready.

ana: thanks. adding sticky note to the release board: "kernel-selector interactions with small-batch traffic — investigate and instrument" :thumbsup:

sam: update: 10% canary looks good — qps up ~8% on canary hosts and p99_token down ~18% there. promoting to 50% now.

ravi: staging results for batching tweak show median latency down 12% for rerank traffic and no throughput regression. I'll try production canary after code review.

miles: PR for dashboard posted: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd123/kernel-batching-kv?orgId=1 (will attach token-stage panels).

ana: great — keep the thread alive with final numbers and we can close once both canary and dashboard are stable.

sam: final prod numbers after 50% promotion: global qps recovered to 226, p99_token back to 98ms, kv_hit_rate steadying at 0.71. leaving selector at conservative mapping for similarity route for now.

ana: marked as mitigated. follow-ups: perf-ci test, long-term solution is better kernel-cost model for selector + per-route config. thanks all. :tada:
